company description: Access Employment Limited (AEL) was established as a Social Enterprise in 1998 as a consequence of high levels of social and economic deprivation in the Larne area.  AEL’s primary objective is to provide employment, work based learning and vocational training for disadvantaged young people and adults, including persons with learning and physical disability, mental health issues and the long term unemployed. AEL believes that everyone should have the opportunity to hold meaningful employment. We champion a mixed ability workforce as it is important for our service users with additional needs to see their peers in achievable valued jobs. This has raised awareness about those living with disabilities, creating disability champions amongst our employees. AEL’s operations are intentionally in an urban, town centre to create a Community Hub, a neutral space accessible to all. AEL has 52 internal employees growing exponentially from 13 and has also successfully placed 26 young people into external employment, culminating in 75 paid job roles being created.   \rAEL operates 7 diverse business areas and 5 employability training programmes. We work in partnership with the NHSCT, surrounding post primary and special educational schools and the NRC to deliver work experience and training through the live businesses of our social enterprise. This enables our service users to sample careers within packaging, manufacturing, online retail, horticulture, and catering. Quality, meaningful work experience enables the trainees to explore their career options, develop their work-related competences, and build on their soft skills, to make more informed decisions about their future progression. AEL generates 70% of its own income and is not reliant on grant funding, which is the sector norm.\rAEL is an ISO 9001 accredited company, which stipulates precise practices within each of the 7 business areas to ensure our business activities meet the highest possible standards of customer service.

headline: Creative Design Director at Slimming World
bio: I've always felt design has more in common with maths than art. Not because creativity is purely logical, but because both start with ‘understanding the problem’. The best briefs don't contain ‘the answer’, they define ‘the problem’. And, once you understand that challenge (trust, clarity, perception, etc), the creative solution often becomes pretty clear and simple: what do you want to say, and how are you going to say it. I've always been drawn to branding over design alone. A brand gives people a reason to believe. It creates an identity, an experience and a philosophy that people recognise, trust and choose. Helping organisations express that authentically has been the focus of my career. Over the last 17 years I've grown alongside Slimming World, progressing from Graphic Designer to Creative Design Director. After leading the company's first major brand evolution developed entirely in-house, I moved into a newly created role focused on stewarding the brand as it continues to grow and evolve. Today I work with internal teams and external agency partners to help ensure every creative decision reflects not just how the brand looks, but reflects what we hold dear. As a designer at heart, inspiration can come from almost anywhere, though I spend as much time learning as I do creating (tip, with a long daily commute you can really rinse Audible). Branding, marketing, leadership, behavioural science and the psychology behind decision-making continue to shape how I think, though (and full circle) it continues to emphasise the paragraph up top: every project just requires ‘understanding the problem’.
